title: AuthorizationRequest
description: The parameters /oauth/authorize accepts, derived from identity_oidc::request::AuthorizationRequest. Every field is a protocol parameter on the request URI, not a JSON body: the endpoint reads them from the query string. This schema documents the parameter NAMES, their requiredness and their accepted values; a JSON document is used because it is the form a checker can validate. x-serde-status records what the Rust type does, so a change in either place is visible in the diff.
x-serde-status: the type is IMPLEMENTED as a shape; the endpoint that would parse it is DEFERRED to phase 4 (OIDC provider)

client_id.description: The client identifier, as registered. Kept as a String in Rust rather than an ApplicationId on purpose: the protocol field is a client-chosen handle, and resolving it to an application is a repository step this type does not perform.

response_type.description: The response type. 'code' is the only value the discovery document advertises (response_types_supported == ["code"]). The implicit and hybrid flows are refused because a token in a redirect is a token in a browser history, a referrer header and a proxy log.

x-accepted-values.constraining: the field is a String in Rust; the code flow is the only supported one, and the constant records it

redirect_uri.description: The client identifier as the USER is redirected back, echoed in the response. Compared EXACTLY against the registered set — never a prefix, never a glob, never normalised. The registered URI must be absolute, http or https, and fragment-free.

x-accepted-values.source: identity_domain::application::Application::allows_redirect_uri; bound and shape rules in Application::add_redirect_uri
x-accepted-values.constraining: the field is a String in Rust; the exact-match rule is the domain's, not the type's

scope.description: Space-delimited scopes. 'openid' is mandatory: a request without it is not an OIDC request. Parsed by splitting on ASCII whitespace and dropping empties; a multi-valued parameter is not how OAuth conveys scopes, so a second parser is not accepted.

x-accepted-values.constraining: the field is a String in Rust; AuthorizationRequest::requests_openid checks membership

state.description: The client's CSRF binding. Required on EVERY request: a request with no state is refused, never defaulted. Not a secret.

nonce.description: The nonce binding the ID token's 'nonce' claim to this request. Its absence from a response to a request that carried one is a replay.
nonce.x-serde-note: Option<String> with no skip_serializing_if and no default attribute, so it is serialised as null when absent and a missing JSON key deserialises to None.

code_challenge.description: The PKCE code challenge, base64url without padding.

code_challenge_method.description: The method the challenge was derived with. 'S256' only. 'plain' is not advertised and is not accepted: advertising a downgrade offer is worse than advertising nothing.

x-accepted-values.constraining: the field is a String in Rust; S256 is the only accepted method

prompt.description: What the user is being asked to consent to. Display-only.
prompt.x-serde-note: Option<String> with no skip_serializing_if and no default attribute.

provider.description: The identity provider to federate to, when the request selects one. A hint about which provider to use, not an assertion from one: an asserted identity enters through AuthenticateExternalIdentity, never through this parameter.
provider.x-serde-note: Option<String> with no skip_serializing_if and no default attribute.

login_hint.description: A pre-filled identifier. Advisory only: a hint is never an assertion and never bypasses a challenge.
login_hint.x-serde-note: Option<String> with no skip_serializing_if and no default attribute.
